# Trial-level regression checks (generated by study/analysis/robustness_mixed.py)

## Experiment 2, the agent task: 16,665 trials, 16 models, 71 cases

| contrast | GEE odds ratio (95% CI) | P | mixed-effects odds ratio (95% CI) |
|---|---|---|---|
| ordering vs implementing | 1.10 (0.81 to 1.48) | 0.535 | 1.18 (1.10 to 1.26) |
| knowledge vs prompt | 2.05 (1.45 to 2.91) | 5.39e-05 | 3.38 (3.08 to 3.71) |
| second record vs prompt | 1.31 (0.98 to 1.76) | 0.0708 | 1.53 (1.42 to 1.66) |

## Experiment 3, the assessment before acting, with the matched agent-task cells as baseline: 16,116 trials, 16 models, 71 cases

| contrast | GEE odds ratio (95% CI) | P | mixed-effects odds ratio (95% CI) |
|---|---|---|---|
| assess vs matched baseline | 0.25 (0.15 to 0.41) | 1.31e-07 | 0.12 (0.09 to 0.14) |
| assess_free vs matched baseline | 0.15 (0.10 to 0.21) | 5.36e-27 | 0.06 (0.05 to 0.07) |
| neutral vs matched baseline | 1.68 (1.23 to 2.28) | 0.00105 | 2.56 (2.24 to 2.93) |
| neutral_free vs matched baseline | 0.55 (0.44 to 0.68) | 2.24e-08 | 0.37 (0.31 to 0.44) |
| assess vs neutral | 0.15 (0.07 to 0.29) | 2.04e-08 | 0.05 (0.03 to 0.06) |

Odds ratios above 1 mean more harmful actions than the reference. The GEE clusters trials by model with an exchangeable working correlation and robust standard errors; the mixed-effects model has random intercepts for model and case, fitted by variational Bayes, with intervals from the posterior standard deviations.
